glyph_origin: Pictogram (象形): a pictogram of a full 橐 (“bag”) tied at both ends. It is the original form of 重: forms with a human figure gave rise to 重, while forms without it gave rise to 東. Interpreted in the Shuowen Jiezi as an ideogrammic compound (會意) the sun (日) rising behind a tree (木). According to Allan (1991) p. 47-50, the character represents the Fu Sang tree. However, the original form is rather different, hence any interpretation tied to a tree is most likely a folk etymology. See the top component of 曹 in the original version. See also 柬, 熏, 西 and 鹵/卤.
s_page_origin: From cursive script of 東; compare 車 → 车.
shuowen: Interpreted in the Shuowen Jiezi as an ideogrammic compound (會意) the sun (日) rising behind a tree (木).
note: glyph_origin is from the traditional page 東; s_page_origin explains the simplified 东.
